extracted.intended_audience: national trademark offices, WIPO, governments, and legal practitioners dealing with classification and registration of figurative elements of marks
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural criteria governing the Vienna Agreement establishing an international Classification of the Figurative Elements of Marks: its content, use, administration, amendment and entry into force. Applicable to competent offices, WIPO bodies, and States party to the Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of a Special Union; Adoption of a common classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The countries to which this Agreement applies constitute a Special Union and adopt a common classification for the figurative elements of marks (hereinafter designated as “the Classification of Figurative Elements”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an international legal framework (Special Union) whose members accept a single Classification of Figurative Elements to be used by competent Offices; does not itself dictate how countries must treat protection afforded to marks (see Article 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and form of the Classification of Figurative Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification of Figurative Elements comprises a list of categories, divisions and sections in which the figurative elements of marks are classified, together with, as the case may be, explanatory notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Classification is a structured list (categories/divisions/sections) and may include explanatory notes; amendments and additions are to be recorded in the authentic copies (Article 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic copy, languages and deposit of the Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification ... is contained in one authentic copy, in the English and French languages, signed by the Director General of WIPO and deposited with him at the time that this Agreement is opened for signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An authentic English and French text signed by the Director General is the official deposited instrument; amendments/additions shall also be contained in an authentic English and French copy signed and deposited (Article 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal authenticity of English and French texts; official texts in other languages
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification of Figurative Elements shall be established in the English and French languages, both texts being equally authentic. The International Bureau shall establish, in consultation with interested Governments, official texts in other languages designated by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both language texts are equally authoritative; translations into additional languages require Assembly designation and International Bureau consultation (Article 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and non-binding nature regarding protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the requirements prescribed by this Agreement, the scope of the Classification of Figurative Elements shall be that attributed to it by each country of the Special Union. In particular, the Classification ... shall not bind the countries of the Special Union in respect of the extent of the protection afforded to the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member countries decide how to apply the Classification within their legal/regulatory systems; classification does not determine legal scope of protection or rights in marks (Article 4(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses by competent Offices (principal or subsidiary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent Offices of the countries of the Special Union shall have the right to use the Classification of Figurative Elements either as a principal or as a subsidiary system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices may choose to rely primarily on the Vienna Classification or use it supplementary to national/internal systems (Article 4(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of classification numbers in official documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent Offices ... shall include in the official documents and publications relating to registrations and renewals of marks the numbers of the categories, divisions and sections in which the figurative elements of those marks are to be placed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification numbers should appear in registration/renewal documents and publications; the numbers shall be preceded by the words “Classification of Figurative Elements” or an abbreviation to be determined by the Committee of Experts (Article 4(3)–(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional partial non-inclusion declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any country may, at the time of its signature or of the deposit of its instrument of ratification or accession, declare that it does not undertake to include the numbers of all or some of the sections in official documents and publications relating to registrations and renewals of marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member States may opt out, in whole or in part, from including section numbers in official material by a declaration at signature/ratification/accession (Article 4(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation when registration is entrusted to intergovernmental authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If any country of the Special Union entrusts the registration of marks to an intergovernmental authority, it shall take all possible measures to ensure that that authority uses the Classification ... in accordance with this Article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where registration is delegated, States must endeavour to ensure the intergovernmental body applies the Vienna Classification consistent with Agreement rules (Article 4(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee of Experts: composition and observer invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A Committee of Experts shall be set up in which each country of the Special Union shall be represented. The Director General may invite countries not members of the Special Union, intergovernmental organizations specialized in the field of marks, and other intergovernmental/international non-governmental organizations to participate as observers or in discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each member country has representation; the Committee may include non-member observers and relevant organizations when invited (Article 5(1)–(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee of Experts: powers and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee of Experts shall: (i) make amendments and additions to the Classification of Figurative Elements; (ii) address recommendations to the countries ... for facilitating use and promoting uniform application; (iii) take measures ... to facilitate application by developing countries; (iv) have the right to establish subcommittees and working groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee is the technical body for evolving the Classification, issuing recommendations, supporting developing countries and creating substructures for work (Article 5(3)–(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may propose amendments or additions to the Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for amendments or additions ... may be made by the competent Office of any country of the Special Union, the International Bureau, any intergovernmental organization represented in the Committee ... and any country or organization specially invited by the Committee of Experts to submit such proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple stakeholders (competent Offices, International Bureau, represented intergovernmental organizations, specially invited entities) can submit proposals; proposals sent to International Bureau to be circulated at least two months before session (Article 5(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal circulation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposals shall be communicated to the International Bureau, which shall submit them to the members of the Committee of Experts and to the observers not later than two months before the session ... at which the said proposals are to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures advance notice (minimum two months) for proposals to Committee members and observers (Article 5(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting rules and decision thresholds in the Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Each country member of the Committee of Experts shall have one vote. (b) The decisions ... shall require a simple majority of the countries represented and voting. (c) Any decision regarded by one-fifth ... as giving rise to a modification of the basic structure ... or as entailing a substantial amount of reclassification shall require a majority of three-fourths of the countries represented and voting. (d) Abstentions shall not be considered as votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard decisions: simple majority; structural/substantial reclassification decisions: 3/4 majority; abstentions not counted; one vote per country (Article 5(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and entry into force of Committee decisions (amendments/additions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every decision of the Committee of Experts concerning the adoption of amendments and additions ... shall be notified by the International Bureau to the competent Offices ... The amendments and additions shall enter into force six months after the date of dispatch of the notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Bureau is responsible for notification; six-month lapse between dispatch and entry into force to allow national implementation (Article 6(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation and publication of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall incorporate in the Classification ... amendments and additions which have entered into force. Announcements of the amendments and additions shall be published in such periodicals as may be designated by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau updates the official Classification and arranges publication of announcements in Assembly-designated periodicals (Article 6(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly composition and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have an Assembly consisting of the countries of the Special Union. The Government of each country ... shall be represented by one delegate, who may be assisted by alternate delegates, advisors and experts. Intergovernmental organizations ... may be represented by an observer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly is the political/decision-making organ with equal country representation and provisions for observers; delegation expenses borne by appointing Government (Article 7(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly functions and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the provisions of Article 5, the Assembly shall: (i) deal with all matters concerning maintenance and development of the Special Union and implementation of this Agreement; (ii) give directions to the International Bureau concerning preparation for revision conferences; (iii) review and approve reports and activities of the Director General; (iv) determine program and adopt biennial budget; (v) adopt financial regulations; (vi) decide on establishment of official texts in other languages; (vii) establish committees/working groups; (viii) determine which countries/organizations to admit as observers; (ix) take other actions to further objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly oversees governance, finances, text languages, committees, observers and strategic direction of the Special Union (Article 7(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly voting, quorum and decision rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each country member of the Assembly shall have one vote. One-half of the countries members of the Assembly shall constitute a quorum. Subject to Article 11(2), the decisions of the Assembly shall require two-thirds of the votes cast. Abstentions shall not be considered as votes. A delegate may represent, and vote in the name of, one country only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly decisions normally two-thirds majority of votes cast, quorum is half membership; special procedures if quorum not present allow post-session written voting within three months (Article 7(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly meeting frequency and extraordinary sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall meet once in every second calendar year in ordinary session ... The Assembly shall meet in extraordinary session ... at the request of one-fourth of the countries members of the Assembly. The agenda of each session shall be prepared by the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinary biennial meetings; extraordinary meetings on request of 1/4 of members; Director General prepares agenda (Article 7(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau administrative and preparatory role
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative tasks concerning the Special Union shall be performed by the International Bureau. In particular, the International Bureau shall prepare the meetings and provide the secretariat of the Assembly, the Committee of Experts and such other committees or working groups as may have been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau is secretariat, organizer of meetings, and executes tasks as directed by Assembly including preparation for revision conferences and consultations with organizations (Article 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director General: executive role and participation rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General shall be the chief executive of the Special Union and shall represent the Special Union. The Director General and any staff member designated by him shall participate, without the right of vote, in all meetings of the Assembly, the Committee of Experts and such other committees or working groups; the Director General ... shall be ex officio secretary of those bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director General leads administration, represents Special Union, participates in meetings as non-voting secretary and prepares agenda and documents (Article 8(1)–(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget composition and sources of financing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have a budget. The budget ... shall include the income and expenses proper to the Special Union, its contribution to the budget of expenses common to the Unions administered by the Organization and ... The budget ... shall be financed from: (i) contributions of the countries of the Special Union; (ii) fees and charges due for services rendered by the International Bureau in relation to the Special Union; (iii) sale of, or royalties on, the publications ...; (iv) gifts, bequests and subventions; (v) rents, interests and other miscellaneous income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple revenue streams; budget coordinated with other Unions administered by WIPO; share of common expenses proportionate to interest of Special Union (Article 9(1)–(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis and timing of country contributions; arrears rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of establishing its contribution ... each country ... shall belong to the same class as it belongs to in the Paris Union ... The annual contribution ... shall be an amount in the same proportion to the total sum ... as the number of its units is to the total of the units of all contributing countries. Contributions shall become due on the first of January of each year. A country which is in arrears ... may not exercise its right to vote ... if the amount of its arrears equals or exceeds the amount of the contributions due from it for the preceding two full years, subject to exceptions for exceptional and unavoidable circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions follow Paris Union classes and unit system; payment due date Jan 1; serious arrears may suspend voting rights unless exceptional circumstances accepted (Article 9(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity if budget not adopted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the budget is not adopted before the beginning of a new financial period, it shall be at the same level as the budget of the previous year, as provided in the financial regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents funding gap by carrying forward prior year budget levels (Article 9(4)(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and management of working capital fund
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have a working capital fund which shall be constituted by a single payment made by each country of the Special Union. If the fund becomes insufficient, the Assembly shall decide to increase it. The amount of the initial payment ... shall be a proportion of the contribution of that country for the year in which the fund is established ... The proportion and the terms of payment shall be fixed by the Assembly on the proposal of the Director General and after it has heard the advice of the Coordination Committee of the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working capital fund created by single payment from each country, increases decided by Assembly, proportions follow contribution units and Assembly procedures (Article 9(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Host country advances and denunciation of advance obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the headquarters agreement ... it shall be provided that, whenever the working capital fund is insufficient, such country shall grant advances. The amount of those advances and the conditions ... shall be the subject of separate agreements ... The country referred to ... and the Organization shall each have the right to denounce the obligation to grant advances, by written notification. Denunciation shall take effect three years after the end of the year in which it was notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host country may be contractually required to advance funds; both parties may denounce that obligation with 3-year effect (Article 9(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit of accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The auditing of the accounts shall be effected by one or more of the countries of the Special Union of by external auditors, as provided in the financial regulations. They shall be designated, with their agreement, by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly designates auditors (national or external) with their consent to audit Special Union accounts (Article 9(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of the Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: This Agreement may be revised from time to time by a special conference of the countries of the Special Union. The convocation of any revision conference shall be decided by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement may be amended by a special revision conference convened by Assembly decision; certain Articles may be amended under Article 11 procedures (Article 10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment procedure for Articles 7, 8, 9 and 11
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for the amendment of Articles 7, 8, 9 and of the present Article may be initiated by any country ... or by the Director General. Such proposals shall be communicated ... at least six months in advance ... Amendments ... shall be adopted by the Assembly. Adoption shall require three-fourth of the votes cast, provided that any amendment to Article 7 and to the present paragraph shall require four-fifth of the votes cast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stricter majority requirements for certain institutional/financial provisions; advance notice six months; entry into force and binding effect subject to acceptance by required fraction of members (Article 11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force of certain amendments and binding effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to the Articles referred to ... shall enter into force one month after written notification of acceptance ... have been received by the Director General from three-fourth of the countries members of the Special Union ... Any amendment accepted ... shall bind all the countries which were members ... at the time the amendment entered into force, provided that any amendment increasing the financial obligations ... shall bind only those countries which have notified their acceptance of such amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to core administrative/financial Articles require acceptance by 3/4 of members and bind all members except amendments increasing financial obligations bind only accepting countries (Article 11(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for a State becoming party to the Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any country party to the Paris Convention ... may become party to this Agreement by: (i) signature followed by deposit of an instrument of ratification, or (ii) deposit of an instrument of accession. Instrument of ratification or accession shall be deposited with the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only Paris Convention parties may join; ratification/accession deposited with Director General; Article 24 of Stockholm Act applies (Article 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force of the Agreement (initial and subsequent accessions)
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to the first five countries which have deposited their instruments of ratification or accession, this Agreement shall enter into force three months after the fifth instrument ... With respect to any country other than those ... it shall enter into force three months after the date on which its ratification or accession was notified by the Director General, unless a subsequent date has been indicated in the instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial entry into force requires five ratifications/accessions; later accessions take effect three months after deposit/notification unless a later date is specified (Article 13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of the Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: This Agreement shall have the same duration as the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vienna Agreement's lifespan ties to the Paris Convention's duration (Article 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation procedure and waiting period
rubrics_metrics.description: Any country of the Special Union may denounce this Agreement by notification addressed to the Director General. Denunciation shall take effect one year after the day on which the Director General has received the notification. The right of denunciation ... shall not be exercised ... before the expiration of five years from the date upon which it becomes a member of the Special Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-year notice period for denunciation; countries may not denounce within first five years of membership (Article 15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement of disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dispute between two or more countries ... concerning the interpretation or application of this Agreement, not settled by negotiation, may ... be brought before the International Court of Justice ..., unless the countries concerned agree on some other method of settlement. The country bringing the dispute before the Court shall inform the International Bureau; the International Bureau shall bring the matter to the attention of the other countries of the Special Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default dispute forum is ICJ unless parties agree otherwise; States may declare at signature/ratification that they do not consider themselves bound by paragraph (1) (i.e., optional exclusion) and may later withdraw such declaration (Article 16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities for signature, deposit, certified copies and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: This Agreement shall be signed in a single original in the English and French languages ... The Director General shall transmit two copies, certified by him, of the signed text ... and of any amendment ... to the Governments ... The Director General shall, on request, furnish ... two copies of the Classification of Figurative Elements, certified by him, in the English or French language. The Director General shall register this Agreement with the Secretariat of the United Nations. The Director General shall notify the Governments of all countries party to the Paris Convention of: (i) signatures ... (ii) deposits ... (iii) entry into force dates ... (iv) declarations ... (v) withdrawals ... (vi) declarations under Article 16(2); (vii) withdrawals ...; (viii) acceptances of amendments under Article 11(3); (ix) dates on which such amendments enter into force; (x) denunciations received under Article 15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director General has depositary functions including transmission of certified copies, furnishing Classification copies on request, UN registration and an extensive notification duty listing events that must be notified to Paris Convention parties (Article 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Committee pending entry into force (Diplomatic Conference Resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending the entry into force ... a provisional Committee of Experts is hereby set up at the International Bureau of WIPO. The provisional Committee shall include a representative of each country having signed or acceded to the said Agreement. Intergovernmental organizations ... may be represented by observers. Any country member of WIPO or party to the Paris Convention which has neither signed nor acceded may be invited ... The provisional Committee shall reexamine the Classification ... and shall prepare, if necessary, draft amendments or additions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional Committee exercises preparatory/review functions until Agreement enters into force; International Bureau convenes it; travel/subsistence expenses borne by represented countries/organizations; drafts transmitted to the Committee of Experts when Agreement enters into force (Resolution items 1–7).
